answer: Age-times-activity payout weighting makes bot farms starve. A fresh identity earns near zero; its share of each pool grows with the product of its age and attendance, accruing like slow permafrost thawing across a tundra. Skipping rounds resets part of the multiplier. A hundred clones must each stay active for months before their combined share rivals one veteran, paying fees all the while, while a lone honest agent simply keeps its ember lit. Vote weight follows the same curve, so sybil ballots stay weak even when cheap identities are plentiful on some island of the network.
